stations.title: Acute Chest Pain — Aortic Dissection
stations.task: Evaluate a patient with acute tearing chest pain and assess for aortic dissection

patient.name: David Thompson
patient.opening: Doctor, I have this tearing pain in my chest that started suddenly an hour ago and is radiating to my back.

keySymptoms: Sudden-onset tearing chest pain radiating to back
Blood pressure differential between arms (180/100 right, 140/80 left)
hiddenProfile.vitalSigns: BP 180/100 (right arm), HR 95, RR 20, O2 sat 96%, Temp 37.1°C

mustAsk: When exactly did the pain start?
What does the pain feel like?
bonus: Ask about family history of Marfan or aortic disease
Check blood pressures in both arms

questions.question: What imaging study confirms the diagnosis?
questions.answer: CT angiogram of the chest (or TEE)
questions.rubric: Identifies appropriate imaging for aortic dissection

stations.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation
stations.task: Evaluate a patient presenting with palpitations and newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation

patient.name: Patricia Moore
patient.opening: My heart has been racing all morning and I feel lightheaded and short of breath.

hiddenProfile.diagnosis: New-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
hiddenProfile.vitalSigns: BP 130/80, HR 140 (irregularly irregular), RR 22, O2 sat 94%

mustAsk: Any chest pain or shortness of breath?
bonus: Ask about alcohol or caffeine intake

questions.question: What is the first step in management?
questions.answer: Rate control with beta-blocker (if no contraindication) and anticoagulation assessment
